title: Kinesis Data Firehose: delivery into S3 without writing code

videos.script: Lesson 20 left Quitanda with a stream of order events that forgets them after a day. {{stream}} The lake has to keep them for years. Somebody could write a program that reads the stream and writes files into S3. Firehose is that program, already written, and you only configure it. {{firehose}} You will create a delivery stream and send it records. Then you will open the objects it wrote and find two orders glued onto one line, because nothing added a newline. {{glued}} Firehose waits before it writes. It gathers records until a size or a time is reached, and that choice decides how many files the lake collects in a day. {{buffer}} It can also name the folders with the date and a field of the record, compress the files, and write Parquet. {{prefix}} moto stores all of that configuration and does almost none of it. You will see exactly which parts, so that the lab never passes for AWS. {{moto}} And you will price it, including a rounding rule that makes small records cost five times their size. {{price}}
